questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 50 kg object is released from rest 2 m above the ground. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its kinetic energy just before impact.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A horizontal force just starts a 20 kg object sliding on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.2. Find the force, using g = 10 m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a connected liquid of uniform density at rest, neglecting capillary effects, which statements are true? I. Pressure acts equally in all directions at a point. II. questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The mass of a specific gravity bottle is 15.2 g when it is empty. It is 24.8 g when filled with kerosene and 27.2 g when filled with distilled water. Calculate the relative density of kerosene.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Convert 78 °C to kelvin, to the nearest kelvin.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Sound travels from the surface to the sea bottom and returns after 4 s. If its speed is 1500 m/s, find the depth.

questions.question: Which change halves the fundamental frequency of a stretched sonometer wire, with other relevant quantities held constant?

options.B: Double its mass at fixed vibrating length and tension

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: To produce a parallel paraxial beam from a concave mirror, where should a small lamp be placed on its principal axis?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A plastic pen rubbed with dry silk attracts a small piece of paper. What happens to the pen and cloth during rubbing?

questions.question: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω supplies two parallel resistors, 12 Ω and 6 Ω. Find the magnitude of current in the 12 Ω resistor.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, which relationship connects pressure P, volume V and absolute temperature T?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solid ammonium chloride is heated to about 350 °C at the closed end of a tube. A porous plug separates it from damp neutral litmus paper near the open end. What happens to the paper initially?
questions.ai_explanation: Heating produces ammonia and hydrogen chloride. Ammonia has the lower molar mass and passes through the porous plug faster. It reaches the damp paper first and produces an alkaline response, turning the paper blue.
questions.explanation: Heating produces ammonia and hydrogen chloride. Ammonia has the lower molar mass and passes through the porous plug faster. It reaches the damp paper first and produces an alkaline response, turning the paper blue.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The colour imparted to a flame by calcium ion is
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.
questions.explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A CuSO₄ cell with copper electrodes and an AgNO₃ cell with silver electrodes are connected in series. After current flows for 10 minutes, 0.63 g of copper is deposited. What mass of silver is deposited in the same period? [Cu = 63, Ag = 108; assume complete current efficiency]
questions.ai_explanation: The copper amount is 0.63/63 = 0.010 mol. Cu²⁺ needs two electrons per atom, so 0.020 mol of electrons passes through both cells. Ag⁺ needs one electron per atom, giving 0.020 × 108 = 2.16 g of silver.
questions.explanation: The copper amount is 0.63/63 = 0.010 mol. Cu²⁺ needs two electrons per atom, so 0.020 mol of electrons passes through both cells. Ag⁺ needs one electron per atom, giving 0.020 × 108 = 2.16 g of silver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In Fe + Cu²⁺ → Fe²⁺ + Cu, iron displaces copper from its ions because

options.A: iron is metallic while copper is ionic
options.B: the atomic weight of copper is greater than that of iron
options.C: copper metal has more electrons than iron metal
options.E: iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper

questions.ai_explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name of CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.ai_explanation: Choose the longest chain containing the double bond: it has four carbon atoms. Number from the double-bond end, giving but-1-ene. The CH₃ branch is on carbon 2, so the name is 2-methylbut-1-ene.
questions.explanation: Choose the longest chain containing the double bond: it has four carbon atoms. Number from the double-bond end, giving but-1-ene. The CH₃ branch is on carbon 2, so the name is 2-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Sodium sulfate decahydrate (Na₂SO₄·10H₂O) loses water of crystallisation on exposure to air. This process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following happens during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.ai_explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.
questions.explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Crude petroleum pollution on creeks and waterways can be dispersed by

options.A: heating the affected water to boil off the petroleum
options.B: mechanically stirring to dissolve petroleum in water
options.C: pouring organic solvents into the water
options.E: cooling to freeze out the petroleum

questions.ai_explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.
questions.explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solutions X, Y and Z have pH values 3.0, 5.0 and 9.0 respectively. Which statement is correct?

options.C: Y and Z are more acidic than water
options.D: Y is more acidic than X

questions.ai_explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.
questions.explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Stainless steel is an alloy containing
questions.ai_explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.50 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ exactly neutralises 20 cm³ of 0.10 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?
questions.ai_explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A student prepares pure Cu(NO₃)₂ crystals starting with CuO. Which reported step is incorrect?

options.A: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
options.C: After cooling, the crystals were separated by filtration
options.D: The crystals were washed with very cold water
options.E: The crystals were allowed to dry

questions.ai_explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.
questions.explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, 3.06 g of KClO₃ saturates 10 cm³ of water. Express the solubility in mol per dm³ of water. [K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.
questions.explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The cracking process is very important in the petroleum industry because it
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.
questions.explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which solution gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?
questions.ai_explanation: CuSO₄ contains sulfate ions, which give white BaSO₄ with barium chloride. Its copper ions produce a blue-green flame. Ammonium sulfate can give the sulfate precipitate but does not give the copper flame colour.
questions.explanation: CuSO₄ contains sulfate ions, which give white BaSO₄ with barium chloride. Its copper ions produce a blue-green flame. Ammonium sulfate can give the sulfate precipitate but does not give the copper flame colour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The mass of an atom is determined by

options.D: the number of neutrons and protons
options.E: the number of neutrons and electrons

questions.ai_explanation: Almost all atomic mass comes from the nucleus. Protons and neutrons each have a mass close to 1 u; electrons contribute very little. The total number of protons and neutrons is the mass number.
questions.explanation: Almost all atomic mass comes from the nucleus. Protons and neutrons each have a mass close to 1 u; electrons contribute very little. The total number of protons and neutrons is the mass number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which addition is an acid–base neutralisation reaction?

options.A: Sodium chloride solution to potassium chloride solution
options.D: Nitric acid to potassium nitrate solution
options.E: Nitric acid to potassium hydroxide solution

questions.ai_explanation: Nitric acid supplies H⁺ ions and potassium hydroxide supplies OH⁻ ions. They combine to form water: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. The overall reaction is HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O, producing potassium nitrate and water.
questions.explanation: Nitric acid supplies H⁺ ions and potassium hydroxide supplies OH⁻ ions. They combine to form water: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. The overall reaction is HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O, producing potassium nitrate and water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Which change greatly increases the rate of this reaction under otherwise identical conditions?

options.B: using a greater volume of acid
options.C: using a smaller volume of acid
options.D: placing the reaction vessel in an ice bath

questions.ai_explanation: Powdered zinc has a larger exposed surface area than the same mass in pellets. More zinc is in contact with the acid at once, so more successful collisions can occur per second.
questions.explanation: Powdered zinc has a larger exposed surface area than the same mass in pellets. More zinc is in contact with the acid at once, so more successful collisions can occur per second.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. How much zinc remains undissolved when 2.00 g of zinc reacts with 10 cm³ of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.
questions.explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: NH₄NO₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O. What volume of nitrogen is produced from 3.20 g of ammonium nitrite at STP? Use a molar gas volume of 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹. [N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.
questions.explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
Which of these elements will not react with either water or steam?
1. Carbon
2. Oxygen
3. Copper
4. Bromine
5. Zinc
questions.ai_explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.
questions.explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Naphthalene melts at 354 K (81 °C). At this temperature its molecules

options.E: become mobile as intermolecular forces holding the solid are overcome

questions.ai_explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.
questions.explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the ratio of the number of molecules in 2 g of hydrogen gas to that in 16 g of oxygen gas? [H = 1, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In which reaction does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
questions.ai_explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.
questions.explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂, which statement describes what happens?

options.E: I⁻ removes an electron from Fe³⁺

questions.ai_explanation: Iodide loses electrons: 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2e⁻. Its oxidation number rises from −1 to 0, so it is oxidised. Each Fe³⁺ ion gains an electron to become Fe²⁺, which is reduction.
questions.explanation: Iodide loses electrons: 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2e⁻. Its oxidation number rises from −1 to 0, so it is oxidised. Each Fe³⁺ ion gains an electron to become Fe²⁺, which is reduction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The energy profile represents A + B → C + D. Which description of the forward reaction follows from it?
questions.ai_explanation: The products lie below the reactants in energy, so the forward reaction releases energy. The approximate change is 40 − 60 = −20 kJ, indicating an exothermic reaction. The profile alone does not establish spontaneity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In dilute solution, NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O has an enthalpy change of −57.3 kJ for the equation as written. Using the same dilute strong-acid/strong-base neutralisation approximation, what is the enthalpy change for 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O?
questions.ai_explanation: The reference reaction forms one mole of water and releases 57.3 kJ. The second equation forms two moles of water. In the stated dilute neutralisation approximation, ΔH = 2 × (−57.3) = −114.6 kJ. The negative sign indicates heat released.
questions.explanation: The reference reaction forms one mole of water and releases 57.3 kJ. The second equation forms two moles of water. In the stated dilute neutralisation approximation, ΔH = 2 × (−57.3) = −114.6 kJ. The negative sign indicates heat released.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Limewater, used to detect carbon dioxide in the laboratory, is an aqueous solution of
questions.ai_explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.
questions.explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is not true of carbon monoxide under ordinary uncatalysed conditions?

options.B: CO is readily oxidised by air at room temperature to form CO₂
options.C: CO can be prepared by passing CO₂ over coke heated to about 1000 °C
options.D: CO can be prepared by heating charcoal with a limited supply of oxygen
options.E: CO is a good reducing agent

questions.ai_explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.
questions.explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: From ZnO + Na₂O → Na₂ZnO₂ and ZnO + CO₂ → ZnCO₃, zinc oxide may be classified as
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc oxide reacts with a basic oxide, Na₂O, and with an acidic oxide, CO₂. An oxide that can show both acidic and basic behaviour is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide reacts with a basic oxide, Na₂O, and with an acidic oxide, CO₂. An oxide that can show both acidic and basic behaviour is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An example of a neutral oxide is
questions.ai_explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 3Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → N₂ + 6HCl, ammonia acts as
questions.ai_explanation: Nitrogen changes from −3 in NH₃ to 0 in N₂, so ammonia is oxidised. The substance that is oxidised reduces the other reactant and is therefore the reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen changes from −3 in NH₃ to 0 in N₂, so ammonia is oxidised. The substance that is oxidised reduces the other reactant and is therefore the reducing agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia, finely divided iron is used as
questions.ai_explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.
questions.explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A compound has vapour density 56.5 relative to hydrogen and composition C 53.1%, N 12.4%, O 28.3%, H 6.2%. What is its molecular formula? [C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen gives molecular mass 2×56.5 = 113. For 100 g, the approximate mole amounts are C:53.1/12, H:6.2/1, O:28.3/16 and N:12.4/14. Dividing by the smallest gives C:H:O:N ≈ 5:7:2:1. C₅H₇O₂N has formula mass 113, so it is also the molecular formula.
questions.explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen gives molecular mass 2×56.5 = 113. For 100 g, the approximate mole amounts are C:53.1/12, H:6.2/1, O:28.3/16 and N:12.4/14. Dividing by the smallest gives C:H:O:N ≈ 5:7:2:1. C₅H₇O₂N has formula mass 113, so it is also the molecular formula.

questions.question: When a kerosene fraction from petroleum is heated strongly and converted into a lower-boiling liquid, the process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.
questions.explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The compound CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH is
questions.ai_explanation: CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH contains a three-carbon chain ending in the carboxyl group, −COOH. The three-carbon carboxylic acid is propanoic acid, not propanol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Alkaline hydrolysis of naturally occurring fats and oils yields.
questions.ai_explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester bonds in fats and oils. It produces glycerol and the sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps.
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester bonds in fats and oils. It produces glycerol and the sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which formula represents a carboxylic acid? R denotes an organic group.
questions.ai_explanation: A carboxylic acid contains the −C(=O)OH group. A has this group; B is an ester, D an acid anhydride, and E an aldehyde. Sulfuric acid in C is not a carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: A carboxylic acid contains the −C(=O)OH group. A has this group; B is an ester, D an acid anhydride, and E an aldehyde. Sulfuric acid in C is not a carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The electricity needed to deposit 1 g of magnesium costs ₦5.00. At the same cost per unit charge and 100% current efficiency, what does it cost to deposit 10 g of aluminium? [Al = 27, Mg = 24]
questions.ai_explanation: Charge per gram is proportional to ionic charge divided by relative atomic mass. For 1 g Mg it is 2/24 mol of electrons; for 10 g Al it is 10×3/27 mol. The charge ratio is (30/27)/(2/24) = 13⅓. At the same cost per unit charge, the cost is ₦5×13⅓ = ₦66.67.
questions.explanation: Charge per gram is proportional to ionic charge divided by relative atomic mass. For 1 g Mg it is 2/24 mol of electrons; for 10 g Al it is 10×3/27 mol. The charge ratio is (30/27)/(2/24) = 13⅓. At the same cost per unit charge, the cost is ₦5×13⅓ = ₦66.67.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Nitrogen can best be obtained from a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen by passing the mixture over
questions.ai_explanation: Heated phosphorus removes oxygen by forming phosphorus oxide, leaving nitrogen. Magnesium is unsuitable because hot magnesium reacts with nitrogen as well as oxygen.
questions.explanation: Heated phosphorus removes oxygen by forming phosphorus oxide, leaving nitrogen. Magnesium is unsuitable because hot magnesium reacts with nitrogen as well as oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Water is said to be ‘hard’ if it

options.B: must be warmed before sodium chloride dissolves
options.C: forms an insoluble scum with soap

questions.ai_explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with soap ions to form insoluble salts, seen as scum. This also makes it harder to obtain a lather.
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with soap ions to form insoluble salts, seen as scum. This also makes it harder to obtain a lather.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH, soluble in excess NaOH. It also gives a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia, soluble in excess ammonia. What is the cation in M?
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc ions form white Zn(OH)₂ with either reagent. The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because it is amphoteric, and in excess ammonia because zinc forms a soluble ammine complex. These two observations identify Zn²⁺.
questions.explanation: Zinc ions form white Zn(OH)₂ with either reagent. The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because it is amphoteric, and in excess ammonia because zinc forms a soluble ammine complex. These two observations identify Zn²⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.ai_explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has four carbon atoms, so the parent is butane. Numbering from the nearer end puts the methyl branch on carbon 2, giving 2-methylbutane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At STP, what volume of hydrogen is formed when 500 cm³ of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ reacts completely with excess zinc? Use a molar gas volume of 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹.

questions.question: How many moles of iron(III) oxide are present in 1.00 kg of the compound? [Fe = 56, O = 16]

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The movement of molecules from the surface of a liquid into the gas phase above it is called
questions.ai_explanation: Evaporation occurs when molecules escape from a liquid surface into the gas phase. Condensation is the reverse change, from gas to liquid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following conducts electricity?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An organic compound contains 72% carbon, 12% hydrogen and 16% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: Take a 100 g sample. The amounts are 72/12 = 6 mol of carbon atoms, 12/1 = 12 mol of hydrogen atoms and 16/16 = 1 mol of oxygen atoms. The simplest whole-number ratio is 6:12:1, giving C₆H₁₂O.
questions.explanation: Take a 100 g sample. The amounts are 72/12 = 6 mol of carbon atoms, 12/1 = 12 mol of hydrogen atoms and 16/16 = 1 mol of oxygen atoms. The simplest whole-number ratio is 6:12:1, giving C₆H₁₂O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Under the same conditions, hydrogen diffuses through a porous plug

options.A: at the same rate as oxygen
options.D: three times as fast as oxygen
options.E: four times as fast as oxygen

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An experiment produces a mixture of CO₂ and CO. Which treatment removes CO₂ while retaining CO?

options.A: Pass it over heated copper(II) oxide
options.B: Bubble it through concentrated sulfuric acid
options.C: Bubble it through sodium hydroxide solution

questions.ai_explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs the acidic oxide CO₂, while CO does not react in this washing step. With sufficient hydroxide, CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Passing the mixture over hot CuO would instead consume CO by oxidising it to CO₂.
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs the acidic oxide CO₂, while CO does not react in this washing step. With sufficient hydroxide, CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Passing the mixture over hot CuO would instead consume CO by oxidising it to CO₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which property identifies chloride ions from an ionic chloride in aqueous solution?

options.A: They can be decomposed by heat
options.B: They react with aqueous AgNO₃ to give a white precipitate soluble in excess ammonia
options.C: They explode on contact with dry ammonia gas
options.D: They react with concentrated sulfuric acid to give white fumes of chlorine gas

questions.explanation: Chloride ions give a white silver chloride precipitate with aqueous silver nitrate: Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s). Excess ammonia dissolves it by forming the soluble complex [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Dilute aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium bromide are mixed and a precipitate forms. Which list gives the resulting solid and dissolved spectator species?
questions.ai_explanation: Lead(II) ions and bromide ions form insoluble lead(II) bromide: Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ → PbBr₂(s). Potassium and nitrate ions remain in solution as spectator ions. The full reaction is Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KBr → PbBr₂ + 2KNO₃.
questions.explanation: Lead(II) ions and bromide ions form insoluble lead(II) bromide: Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ → PbBr₂(s). Potassium and nitrate ions remain in solution as spectator ions. The full reaction is Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KBr → PbBr₂ + 2KNO₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Bronze is an alloy of

questions.explanation: Traditional bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Copper and zinc form brass, which is a different alloy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to give which set of products?
questions.ai_explanation: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises copper to copper(II) nitrate and is reduced mainly to nitrogen dioxide. The balanced equation is Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.
questions.explanation: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises copper to copper(II) nitrate and is reduced mainly to nitrogen dioxide. The balanced equation is Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Al₂O₃(s) + 3H₂SO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l). Al₂O₃(s) + 2NaOH(aq) + 3H₂O(l) → 2NaAl(OH)₄(aq). These reactions show that Al₂O₃ is
questions.ai_explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with sulfuric acid and also with sodium hydroxide. An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with sulfuric acid and also with sodium hydroxide. An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The fraction of crude oil used as jet fuel is
questions.ai_explanation: The kerosene fraction is used to produce common aviation turbine fuels such as Jet A and Jet A-1. Refinery gas and gasoline are lighter fractions, while diesel is a heavier fuel fraction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why is tetraethyllead undesirable as an antiknock additive?

options.B: It causes pollution through exhaust emissions
options.C: It lowers the octane rating of petrol

questions.ai_explanation: Tetraethyllead improves resistance to engine knocking, but burning leaded fuel releases lead-containing pollution in the exhaust. This environmental contamination is the reason for avoiding it as an antiknock additive.

questions.question: The carbon atoms in ethane are

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Palm wine turns sour with time because

options.A: Its sugar content is converted into alcohol
options.B: The carbon dioxide formed during fermentation has a sour taste
options.C: It is commonly adulterated by tappers and sellers
options.D: Microbial activity produces organic acids in it

questions.explanation: Microorganisms produce organic acids during continued palm-wine fermentation. For example, acetic-acid bacteria can oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid, increasing acidity and producing a sour taste.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 8 g of CH₄ occupies 11.2 dm³ at s.t.p. What volume would 22 g of CH₃CH₂CH₃ occupy under the same conditions? [C = 12, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: CH₄ has molar mass 16 g mol⁻¹, so 8 g contains 0.5 mol. CH₃CH₂CH₃ has molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹, so 22 g also contains 0.5 mol. Equal amounts of gas occupy equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure: 11.2 dm³.
questions.explanation: CH₄ has molar mass 16 g mol⁻¹, so 8 g contains 0.5 mol. CH₃CH₂CH₃ has molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹, so 22 g also contains 0.5 mol. Equal amounts of gas occupy equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure: 11.2 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: To what temperature must a fixed amount of gas initially at 273 K be heated to double both its volume and pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of gas, PV/T is constant. Doubling both pressure and volume multiplies PV by four, so the absolute temperature must become 4 × 273 = 1092 K.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas, PV/T is constant. Doubling both pressure and volume multiplies PV by four, so the absolute temperature must become 4 × 273 = 1092 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A gas has relative molecular mass 2Y. Using the hydrogen-reference convention for vapour density, what is Y?

options.B: The vapour density of the gas

questions.ai_explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen compares the masses of equal gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure. Since hydrogen has relative molecular mass 2, Mr = 2 × vapour density. Thus Y is the vapour density.
questions.explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen compares the masses of equal gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure. Since hydrogen has relative molecular mass 2, Mr = 2 × vapour density. Thus Y is the vapour density.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At the same temperature and pressure, gases X and Y have densities 0.5 g dm⁻³ and 2.0 g dm⁻³ respectively. What is the rate of diffusion of X relative to Y?
questions.ai_explanation: By Graham’s law, diffusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of gas density under the same conditions. Hence rate(X)/rate(Y) = √(2.0/0.5) = √4 = 2.0.
questions.explanation: By Graham’s law, diffusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of gas density under the same conditions. Hence rate(X)/rate(Y) = √(2.0/0.5) = √4 = 2.0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Heating a gas in a fixed-volume container increases its pressure because

options.A: It decreases the number of collisions between molecules
options.B: The gas molecules bombard the container walls more frequently
options.C: It increases the number of collisions between molecules
options.D: It causes the molecules to combine

questions.ai_explanation: Heating increases the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules. In a fixed-volume container they strike its walls more frequently and with greater momentum, increasing the pressure.
questions.explanation: Heating increases the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules. In a fixed-volume container they strike its walls more frequently and with greater momentum, increasing the pressure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of these properties generally decreases down a group in the periodic table?
questions.ai_explanation: Down a group, additional electron shells increase shielding and the distance between the nucleus and bonding electrons. Electronegativity therefore generally decreases. Atomic size and electropositivity generally increase.
questions.explanation: Down a group, additional electron shells increase shielding and the distance between the nucleus and bonding electrons. Electronegativity therefore generally decreases. Atomic size and electropositivity generally increase.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which option gives the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons, respectively, in a neutral deuterium atom?
questions.ai_explanation: Deuterium is hydrogen-2. A neutral deuterium atom has one proton, one neutron and one electron, giving mass number 2 and atomic number 1.
questions.explanation: Deuterium is hydrogen-2. A neutral deuterium atom has one proton, one neutron and one electron, giving mass number 2 and atomic number 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A stoppered U-tube contains anhydrous calcium chloride. A known volume of air enters through one side, passes through the calcium chloride, and leaves through the other side. This apparatus is useful for determining the amount of
questions.ai_explanation: Anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs water vapour. Passing a known volume of air through the tube allows the absorbed water to be determined from its mass gain, so the apparatus measures water vapour in air.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is a base?
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium oxide is a basic oxide: it neutralises acids to form a salt and water, for example CaO + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O. CO₂ is an acidic oxide, while H₃PO₃ and CH₃COOH are acids.
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide is a basic oxide: it neutralises acids to form a salt and water, for example CaO + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O. CO₂ is an acidic oxide, while H₃PO₃ and CH₃COOH are acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of oxygen at s.t.p. is liberated by 9650 C during electrolysis, assuming the charge is used for oxygen evolution? [Molar gas volume = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹; F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: Producing one mole of O₂ from water or hydroxide requires four moles of electrons. The charge supplies 9650/96500 = 0.100 mol electrons, giving 0.0250 mol O₂. At s.t.p., its volume is 0.0250 × 22.4 = 0.560 dm³.
questions.explanation: Producing one mole of O₂ from water or hydroxide requires four moles of electrons. The charge supplies 9650/96500 = 0.100 mol electrons, giving 0.0250 mol O₂. At s.t.p., its volume is 0.0250 × 22.4 = 0.560 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In electrolytic purification using a copper(II) chloride solution, crude copper should be

options.A: Both the anode and the cathode

questions.ai_explanation: The impure copper is the anode, where copper dissolves by oxidation: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻. Copper ions are reduced and deposited on a separate cathode. This transfers copper away from the impure electrode.
questions.explanation: The impure copper is the anode, where copper dissolves by oxidation: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻. Copper ions are reduced and deposited on a separate cathode. This transfers copper away from the impure electrode.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: H⁻ + H₂O(l) → H₂(g) + OH⁻(aq). What can be inferred?

options.A: The reaction is a double decomposition
options.B: The hydride ion is a reducing agent
options.C: The hydride ion is an oxidising agent

questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen in H⁻ has oxidation number −1 and becomes 0 in H₂. The hydride ion is oxidised, so it acts as the reducing agent. Hydrogen from water is reduced from +1 to 0.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen in H⁻ has oxidation number −1 and becomes 0 in H₂. The hydride ion is oxidised, so it acts as the reducing agent. Hydrogen from water is reduced from +1 to 0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: MnO₄⁻(aq) + 8H⁺(aq) + 5Fe²⁺(aq) → Mn²⁺(aq) + 5Fe³⁺(aq) + 4H₂O(l). How does the oxidation number of manganese change?

questions.explanation: In MnO₄⁻, four oxygen atoms contribute −8. The ion has charge −1, so manganese is +7. In Mn²⁺ it is +2, giving a change from +7 to +2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is true for an exothermic reaction at equilibrium?

options.A: Increasing temperature increases the equilibrium constant
options.B: Increasing temperature decreases the equilibrium constant
options.C: Adding a catalyst increases the equilibrium constant
options.D: Adding a catalyst decreases the equilibrium constant

questions.ai_explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature favours the reverse, endothermic direction. The equilibrium constant for the forward reaction decreases. A catalyst changes the rate of reaching equilibrium but not the equilibrium constant.
questions.explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature favours the reverse, endothermic direction. The equilibrium constant for the forward reaction decreases. A catalyst changes the rate of reaching equilibrium but not the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: Which solution gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution acidified with hydrochloric acid?

questions.question: Why is SO₃ not dissolved directly in water during manufacture of H₂SO₄ by the Contact process?

options.B: Acid is usually added to water, never water to acid
options.C: SO₃ does not dissolve readily in water

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In an electrolytic arrangement used to protect iron from corrosion, the iron is

questions.question: When sodium is added to ethanol, the products are

questions.question: The general formula of alkanones is

questions.question: When sodium ethanoate is treated with a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid, one product is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which reaction represents saponification?

options.A: Carboxylic acids reacting with sodium hydroxide
options.D: Alkanoate esters reacting with sodium hydroxide

questions.ai_explanation: Saponification is alkaline hydrolysis of an ester. An alkanoate ester reacts with sodium hydroxide to form a sodium carboxylate and an alcohol: RCOOR′ + NaOH → RCOONa + R′OH. Fats give soap and glycerol because they are glycerol esters.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many H⁺ ions can 4.9 g of H₂SO₄ provide if both acidic hydrogens are completely released? [S = 32, O = 16, H = 1; Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹]

questions.question: What volume of oxygen remains after complete reaction of 8 cm³ of hydrogen with 20 cm³ of oxygen, with all gas volumes compared at the same temperature and pressure?

questions.question: The stability of ionic solids is generally due to the

options.A: negative electron affinity of most atoms

questions.question: Deliquescent substances are also

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes colloids from suspensions under ordinary standing conditions? Colloids…

options.B: can be separated by filtration, whereas suspensions cannot

questions.question: What is the pH of a 2.50 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ NaOH solution at 25 °C?

questions.explanation: Chloride ions lose electrons in 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Electron loss is oxidation, and chlorine’s oxidation number increases from −1 to 0.

questions.ai_explanation: Magnesium and calcium are highly reactive metals for which electrolysis of molten compounds is an established extraction route. Zinc, copper and lead can be obtained by chemical reduction routes instead.
questions.explanation: Magnesium and calcium are highly reactive metals for which electrolysis of molten compounds is an established extraction route. Zinc, copper and lead can be obtained by chemical reduction routes instead.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed metal becomes passive in concentrated nitric acid?
questions.ai_explanation: Concentrated nitric acid can make iron passive by producing a protective surface film that greatly slows further attack. This is the standard iron passivation example.
questions.explanation: Concentrated nitric acid can make iron passive by producing a protective surface film that greatly slows further attack. This is the standard iron passivation example.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When excess ethanol is heated to 145 °C in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄, the main organic product is
questions.ai_explanation: At about 140–145 °C with excess ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid, intermolecular dehydration produces diethyl ether: 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. Higher temperatures favour ethene formation.
questions.explanation: At about 140–145 °C with excess ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid, intermolecular dehydration produces diethyl ether: 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. Higher temperatures favour ethene formation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many grams of bromine are required for complete addition to 5.2 g of but-1-en-3-yne? [C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80]
questions.ai_explanation: But-1-en-3-yne is CH₂=CH–C≡CH, with formula C₄H₄ and molar mass 52 g mol⁻¹. One C=C bond consumes one Br₂ and one C≡C consumes two Br₂ on full addition. Thus 5.2/52 × 3 × 160 = 48.0 g bromine is required.
questions.explanation: But-1-en-3-yne is CH₂=CH–C≡CH, with formula C₄H₄ and molar mass 52 g mol⁻¹. One C=C bond consumes one Br₂ and one C≡C consumes two Br₂ on full addition. Thus 5.2/52 × 3 × 160 = 48.0 g bromine is required.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Polyvinyl chloride is commonly used to produce
questions.ai_explanation: Polyvinyl chloride is a durable thermoplastic widely used for pipes. Its long polymer chains and material properties suit this use.
questions.explanation: Polyvinyl chloride is a durable thermoplastic widely used for pipes. Its long polymer chains and material properties suit this use.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When the two terminal alkyl groups of ethyl ethanoate are interchanged, the compound formed is
questions.ai_explanation: Ethyl ethanoate is CH₃–C(=O)–O–C₂H₅. Swapping the terminal methyl and ethyl groups gives C₂H₅–C(=O)–O–CH₃. The alcohol-derived group is methyl and the acid-derived part has three carbons, so the ester is methyl propanoate.
questions.explanation: Ethyl ethanoate is CH₃–C(=O)–O–C₂H₅. Swapping the terminal methyl and ethyl groups gives C₂H₅–C(=O)–O–CH₃. The alcohol-derived group is methyl and the acid-derived part has three carbons, so the ester is methyl propanoate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Knowledge of radioactive half-life can help to
questions.ai_explanation: A radioactive isotope has a characteristic half-life. Measuring decay and comparing it with known data can help identify or detect a radionuclide; knowing its half-life does not itself create, split or irradiate atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The molecular shapes of CO₂, H₂O and CH₄, respectively, are
questions.ai_explanation: CO₂ has two electron-domain directions around carbon and is linear. H₂O has two bonds and two lone pairs around oxygen, giving a bent molecular shape. CH₄ has four bonding domains and is tetrahedral.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed pollutant is a synthetic pesticide rather than a product of natural environmental processes?
questions.ai_explanation: DDT is a manufactured organochlorine pesticide. Nitric oxide, carbon monoxide and formaldehyde can be produced by natural processes, whereas DDT contamination originates from its human manufacture and use.
questions.explanation: DDT is a manufactured organochlorine pesticide. Nitric oxide, carbon monoxide and formaldehyde can be produced by natural processes, whereas DDT contamination originates from its human manufacture and use.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Hydration of ions is associated with
questions.ai_explanation: When gaseous ions become surrounded by water molecules, favourable ion–dipole attractions form and energy is released. Hydration itself is exothermic, although dissolving an entire solid also requires energy to separate its lattice.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In HCl(aq) + H₂O(l) → H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), what is Cl⁻ in relation to HCl?
questions.ai_explanation: HCl donates a proton to water. The species left after that donation, Cl⁻, is the conjugate base of HCl; H₃O⁺ is the conjugate acid of water.
questions.explanation: HCl donates a proton to water. The species left after that donation, Cl⁻, is the conjugate base of HCl; H₃O⁺ is the conjugate acid of water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Using the ideal concentration model at 25 °C, what is the pOH of 0.25 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid?
questions.ai_explanation: For fully dissociated HCl, [H⁺] = 0.25 mol dm⁻³. Thus pH = −log₁₀(0.25) = 0.602 and, at 25 °C in the ideal dilute-solution model, pOH = 14.00 − 0.602 = 13.40.
questions.explanation: For fully dissociated HCl, [H⁺] = 0.25 mol dm⁻³. Thus pH = −log₁₀(0.25) = 0.602 and, at 25 °C in the ideal dilute-solution model, pOH = 14.00 − 0.602 = 13.40.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Complete the reduction half-equation: MnO₄⁻(aq) + 8H⁺(aq) + Y → Mn²⁺(aq) + 4H₂O(l). What is Y?
questions.ai_explanation: Manganese changes from +7 in MnO₄⁻ to +2, gaining five electrons. The balanced half-equation is MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, with equal charge and atoms on both sides.
questions.explanation: Manganese changes from +7 in MnO₄⁻ to +2, gaining five electrons. The balanced half-equation is MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, with equal charge and atoms on both sides.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For the stoichiometric amounts in ½Zn²⁺(aq) + e⁻ → ½Zn(s), what charge is required to deposit ½ mol Zn? [F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The half-equation uses one mole of electrons for half a mole of Zn. Its charge is therefore one Faraday: Q = 1 × 96,500 = 9.650 × 10⁴ C.
questions.explanation: The half-equation uses one mole of electrons for half a mole of Zn. Its charge is therefore one Faraday: Q = 1 × 96,500 = 9.650 × 10⁴ C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: If M is deposited mass, Q is charge passed and Z is the electrochemical equivalent, how is Faraday’s first law written?
questions.ai_explanation: Faraday’s first law states that deposited mass is proportional to charge. The electrochemical equivalent Z is mass deposited per unit charge, so M = ZQ. Its units give (g C⁻¹) × C = g.
questions.explanation: Faraday’s first law states that deposited mass is proportional to charge. The electrochemical equivalent Z is mass deposited per unit charge, so M = ZQ. Its units give (g C⁻¹) × C = g.

questions.question: For equal masses under the same conditions, powdered marble reacts faster with hydrochloric acid than granular marble because the powder has

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which rate-versus-concentration plot represents a zero-order reaction?

options.A: A straight-line rise followed by a straight-line fall
options.B: A horizontal line at a positive rate
options.C: A straight line rising from the origin
options.D: A curved rise that reaches a maximum and then falls

questions.explanation: A zero-order reaction has rate = k, independent of reactant concentration over the range where that rate law applies. Its rate-versus-concentration plot is therefore horizontal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the usual equilibrium-constant expression, which species contribute variable concentration or partial-pressure terms?
questions.ai_explanation: In the usual concentration or pressure equilibrium expression, gaseous and dissolved species contribute variable terms. Pure solids and pure liquids have effectively constant activities and are absorbed into the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: According to the standard electrochemical reactivity series, which metal is least readily oxidised?
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc has a less negative standard reduction potential than aluminium, sodium or calcium, so it has the lowest thermodynamic tendency to be oxidised among these metals. questions.question: Which gas sample contains the fewest atoms at standard temperature and pressure?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A heating curve shows a solid warming, a melting plateau, liquid warming to 150 °C, a liquid–vapour plateau at 150 °C, then further warming of the vapour. If this vapour is cooled at the same pressure, at what temperature does condensation begin?

options.D: It necessarily increases at constant pressure

questions.question: Which aqueous solution forms a precipitate when a small amount of NaOH solution is added?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a limited amount of hydroxide to aluminium chloride forms white Al(OH)₃: Al³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Al(OH)₃(s). The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Adding a limited amount of hydroxide to aluminium chloride forms white Al(OH)₃: Al³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Al(OH)₃(s). The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of an alkene with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst is
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen adds across the alkene C=C bond in the presence of a suitable catalyst. The carbon skeleton remains intact and a saturated alkane forms, so this is an addition reaction.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the alkene C=C bond in the presence of a suitable catalyst. The carbon skeleton remains intact and a saturated alkane forms, so this is an addition reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The intermediate formed when ethanol is progressively oxidised to ethanoic acid using acidified potassium dichromate is
questions.ai_explanation: Ethanol first oxidises to ethanal, CH₃CHO. Further oxidation converts the aldehyde group into the carboxylic acid group of ethanoic acid.
questions.explanation: Ethanol first oxidises to ethanal, CH₃CHO. Further oxidation converts the aldehyde group into the carboxylic acid group of ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ is a
questions.ai_explanation: In CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, the carbon bearing OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms and one hydrogen. It is therefore a secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol.
questions.explanation: In CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, the carbon bearing OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms and one hydrogen. It is therefore a secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the specific name for boiling fat with aqueous caustic soda to produce soap?
questions.ai_explanation: Boiling a fat with aqueous sodium hydroxide breaks its ester bonds to form glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps. This specific alkaline hydrolysis is called saponification.
questions.explanation: Boiling a fat with aqueous sodium hydroxide breaks its ester bonds to form glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps. This specific alkaline hydrolysis is called saponification.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ordinary soda-lime glass is manufactured from silica, CaCO₃ and
questions.ai_explanation: Soda-lime glass is made using silica, limestone and sodium carbonate. Sodium carbonate supplies sodium oxide in the melt and acts as a flux, lowering the temperature needed to process silica.
questions.explanation: Soda-lime glass is made using silica, limestone and sodium carbonate. Sodium carbonate supplies sodium oxide in the melt and acts as a flux, lowering the temperature needed to process silica.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed element is especially noted for extensive catenation into long chains and rings?
questions.ai_explanation: Carbon forms strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, supporting extensive chains, branched structures and rings. This extensive catenation is central to organic chemistry.
questions.explanation: Carbon forms strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, supporting extensive chains, branched structures and rings. This extensive catenation is central to organic chemistry.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol can be produced from starch by
questions.ai_explanation: Starch is first hydrolysed into fermentable sugars. Yeast can then convert those sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Distillation separates ethanol after production but does not convert starch into ethanol.
questions.explanation: Starch is first hydrolysed into fermentable sugars. Yeast can then convert those sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Distillation separates ethanol after production but does not convert starch into ethanol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium is sufficiently reactive to release hydrogen from aqueous hydrochloric acid, producing sodium chloride. Silver, gold and copper do not displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidising hydrochloric acid under ordinary conditions.
questions.explanation: Sodium is sufficiently reactive to release hydrogen from aqueous hydrochloric acid, producing sodium chloride. Silver, gold and copper do not displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidising hydrochloric acid under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement about a proton is correct?

options.B: Its mass is one-twelfth the molar mass of carbon
options.C: Its mass is approximately 1840 times the mass of an electron
options.D: The total mass of the protons in any nucleus is always half its nuclear mass

questions.ai_explanation: A proton is about 1836 times as massive as an electron, often rounded to 1840 in school calculations. Its mass is about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁴ g. A molar mass describes one mole, not one particle, and nuclei do not all have equal numbers of protons and neutrons.
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1836 times as massive as an electron, often rounded to 1840 in school calculations. Its mass is about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁴ g. A molar mass describes one mole, not one particle, and nuclei do not all have equal numbers of protons and neutrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the beta-minus decay ¹⁴₆C → X + β⁻, which nuclide is X?
questions.ai_explanation: In beta-minus decay a neutron changes into a proton, so atomic number increases by one while mass number stays the same. Carbon-14, with atomic number 6, becomes nitrogen-14 with atomic number 7.
questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay a neutron changes into a proton, so atomic number increases by one while mass number stays the same. Carbon-14, with atomic number 6, becomes nitrogen-14 with atomic number 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which chloride has the least ionic character?
questions.ai_explanation: Al³⁺ has high charge and small size, giving strong polarising power. It distorts the chloride electron cloud, increasing covalent character; AlCl₃ is therefore the least ionic of these choices.
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ has high charge and small size, giving strong polarising power. It distorts the chloride electron cloud, increasing covalent character; AlCl₃ is therefore the least ionic of these choices.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Processes that return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere include
questions.ai_explanation: Respiration, aerobic decomposition and combustion release carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis instead takes up CO₂, and transpiration chiefly releases water vapour.
questions.explanation: Respiration, aerobic decomposition and combustion release carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis instead takes up CO₂, and transpiration chiefly releases water vapour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which Dalton postulate is retained in the modern description of stoichiometric compounds?

options.A: All elements consist of indivisible particles
options.B: Atoms of different elements combine in simple whole-number ratios
options.C: Atoms can never be created or destroyed in any process
options.D: All atoms of the same element are exactly alike

questions.ai_explanation: Atoms combine in whole-number ratios in the formulas of stoichiometric compounds. Atoms have subatomic structure, isotopes of an element need not be identical in mass, and nuclear processes can transform atoms, so those absolute older claims require revision.
questions.explanation: Atoms combine in whole-number ratios in the formulas of stoichiometric compounds. Atoms have subatomic structure, isotopes of an element need not be identical in mass, and nuclear processes can transform atoms, so those absolute older claims require revision.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A non-reacting ideal-gas mixture contains 0.75 mol cyclopropane and 0.66 mol oxygen at total pressure 0.7 atm. What is the partial pressure of oxygen?
questions.ai_explanation: The oxygen mole fraction is 0.66/(0.75 + 0.66) = 0.4681. Dalton’s law gives p(O₂) = 0.4681 × 0.7 = 0.3277 atm, or 0.33 atm.
questions.explanation: The oxygen mole fraction is 0.66/(0.75 + 0.66) = 0.4681. Dalton’s law gives p(O₂) = 0.4681 × 0.7 = 0.3277 atm, or 0.33 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When H₂S reduces aqueous iron(III) chloride, the resulting iron-ion solution is
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen sulfide reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, whose aqueous solution is pale green: 2Fe³⁺ + H₂S → 2Fe²⁺ + S + 2H⁺. Sulfur also separates as a solid.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, whose aqueous solution is pale green: 2Fe³⁺ + H₂S → 2Fe²⁺ + S + 2H⁺. Sulfur also separates as a solid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which condition specifically indicates chemical equilibrium at fixed temperature and pressure? Here ΔᵣG is the reaction Gibbs energy at the current composition.
questions.ai_explanation: At equilibrium, the reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG is zero, so neither direction has a thermodynamic driving force. This does not require the standard reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG° to be zero.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG is zero, so neither direction has a thermodynamic driving force. This does not require the standard reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG° to be zero.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For Cu₂S(s) + O₂(g) → 2Cu(s) + SO₂(g), how does copper’s oxidation number change?
questions.ai_explanation: Sulfide has oxidation number −2 in Cu₂S, so each copper is +1. Elemental copper has oxidation number 0, giving the change +1 → 0.
questions.explanation: Sulfide has oxidation number −2 in Cu₂S, so each copper is +1. Elemental copper has oxidation number 0, giving the change +1 → 0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Electrolysis of dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide using platinum electrodes produces
questions.ai_explanation: With inert platinum electrodes, water is reduced to hydrogen at the cathode and hydroxide is oxidised to oxygen at the anode. The net change is 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
questions.explanation: With inert platinum electrodes, water is reduced to hydrogen at the cathode and hydroxide is oxidised to oxygen at the anode. The net change is 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), which statement describes the equilibrium shift when pressure is decreased by expansion at fixed temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole on the reactant side. Expansion at fixed temperature lowers pressure and favours the products, increasing the equilibrium amount of PCl₃.
questions.explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole on the reactant side. Expansion at fixed temperature lowers pressure and favours the products, increasing the equilibrium amount of PCl₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The Arrhenius equation relates a reaction’s rate constant to temperature and its
questions.ai_explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which description gives the thermal effect when NaOH flakes dissolve in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.
questions.explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Water vapour changes anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride from
questions.ai_explanation: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue. On taking up water it forms hydrated species that appear pink, producing the blue-to-pink change used in a water test.
questions.explanation: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue. On taking up water it forms hydrated species that appear pink, producing the blue-to-pink change used in a water test.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 20 °C, a salt of molar mass 101 g mol⁻¹ has solubility 0.34 mol dm⁻³. If 3.40 g dissolves in 250 cm³ of water with negligible volume change, the solution is
questions.ai_explanation: The amount is 3.40/101 = 0.0337 mol. With negligible volume change, concentration is 0.0337/0.250 = 0.135 mol dm⁻³, below the solubility of 0.34 mol dm⁻³. More salt can dissolve, so the solution is unsaturated.
questions.explanation: The amount is 3.40/101 = 0.0337 mol. With negligible volume change, concentration is 0.0337/0.250 = 0.135 mol dm⁻³, below the solubility of 0.34 mol dm⁻³. More salt can dissolve, so the solution is unsaturated.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 25 cm³ of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ Na₂CO₃ requires 20 cm³ of HCl for complete neutralisation. What is the HCl concentration?
questions.ai_explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate amount is 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.010 mol HCl. The acid concentration is 0.010/0.020 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate amount is 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.010 mol HCl. The acid concentration is 0.010/0.020 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a hydrated salt loses water of crystallisation on exposure to air, the process is called
questions.ai_explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. Deliquescence instead involves absorbing moisture until the solid dissolves.
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. Deliquescence instead involves absorbing moisture until the solid dissolves.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Three drops of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH are added to 20 cm³ of an aqueous solution at pH 8.4. The resulting pH will be

options.D: Close to that of pure water

questions.ai_explanation: Adding concentrated sodium hydroxide increases the hydroxide concentration and decreases the hydrogen-ion concentration. The resulting pH is greater than 8.4.
questions.explanation: Adding concentrated sodium hydroxide increases the hydroxide concentration and decreases the hydrogen-ion concentration. The resulting pH is greater than 8.4.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which interaction chiefly explains why a small alcohol such as ethanol mixes readily with water?
questions.ai_explanation: The OH group in a small alcohol such as ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water. This favours mixing; solubility decreases as the non-polar carbon chain becomes longer.
questions.explanation: The OH group in a small alcohol such as ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water. This favours mixing; solubility decreases as the non-polar carbon chain becomes longer.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Calcium carbonate scale formed when temporary hard water is boiled comes from dissolved
questions.ai_explanation: On heating, dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate decomposes: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃(s) + CO₂ + H₂O. Insoluble calcium carbonate coats the kettle as scale.
questions.explanation: On heating, dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate decomposes: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃(s) + CO₂ + H₂O. Insoluble calcium carbonate coats the kettle as scale.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 3Cu + pHNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + xNO, what are p and x respectively?
questions.ai_explanation: Three copper atoms lose six electrons in total. Two nitrate nitrogen atoms each gain three electrons to form NO; six further nitrate groups remain with copper. Balancing H and O gives 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Neon and the heavier noble gases owe their low reactivity largely to their
questions.ai_explanation: Neon and the heavier noble gases have eight outer-shell electrons, a stable octet. Helium is a separate case with its first shell filled by two electrons.
questions.explanation: Neon and the heavier noble gases have eight outer-shell electrons, a stable octet. Helium is a separate case with its first shell filled by two electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: According to kinetic theory, increasing absolute temperature causes average kinetic energy of gas particles to
questions.ai_explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to absolute temperature: average Eₖ = 3kT/2. Increasing temperature therefore increases their average kinetic energy.
questions.explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to absolute temperature: average Eₖ = 3kT/2. Increasing temperature therefore increases their average kinetic energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When cathode rays are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, the instrument becomes
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. Collection of these electrons by the electrometer electrode adds negative charge.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. Collection of these electrons by the electrometer electrode adds negative charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed interaction is ordinarily the weakest individual attraction?
questions.ai_explanation: Van der Waals interactions are generally much weaker individually than ordinary ionic or covalent bonds. Coordinate covalent bonds are also covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: Van der Waals interactions are generally much weaker individually than ordinary ionic or covalent bonds. Coordinate covalent bonds are also covalent bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which ion acts as an acid in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Hydronium, H₃O⁺, donates a proton in aqueous acid-base reactions. K⁺ and NO₃⁻ do not appreciably acidify water, while S²⁻ acts as a base.
questions.explanation: Hydronium, H₃O⁺, donates a proton in aqueous acid-base reactions. K⁺ and NO₃⁻ do not appreciably acidify water, while S²⁻ acts as a base.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which method can biologically help decontaminate farmland affected by crude-oil spillage?
questions.ai_explanation: Suitable aerobic bacteria break down some petroleum hydrocarbons in the presence of oxygen. This bioremediation requires appropriate conditions and does not instantly remove every oil component.
questions.explanation: Suitable aerobic bacteria break down some petroleum hydrocarbons in the presence of oxygen. This bioremediation requires appropriate conditions and does not instantly remove every oil component.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For an equilibrium whose forward reaction has ΔH > 0, which temperature change favours the forward equilibrium direction?
questions.ai_explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic when ΔH is positive. Raising temperature favours the heat-absorbing direction and shifts equilibrium towards products.
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic when ΔH is positive. Raising temperature favours the heat-absorbing direction and shifts equilibrium towards products.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The defining feature of an anode reaction is that
questions.ai_explanation: Oxidation occurs at the anode: a species loses electrons. An anode may dissolve if it is an active metal, but dissolution is not required for every anode reaction.
questions.explanation: Oxidation occurs at the anode: a species loses electrons. An anode may dissolve if it is an active metal, but dissolution is not required for every anode reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which quantity changes when a catalyst provides an alternative pathway?
questions.ai_explanation: A catalyst provides a pathway with lower activation energy. It does not alter the energies of starting reactants and final products, so reaction enthalpy is unchanged.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a pathway with lower activation energy. It does not alter the energies of starting reactants and final products, so reaction enthalpy is unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: If Y is an oxidizing agent that reacts with a reducing agent, Z, which of the following is correct?
questions.ai_explanation: An oxidising agent accepts electrons and is reduced. Thus Y is reduced while reducing agent Z loses electrons and is oxidised.
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent accepts electrons and is reduced. Thus Y is reduced while reducing agent Z loses electrons and is oxidised.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes, which pair represents cathode and anode discharge respectively in introductory ion-discharge notation?
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen forms at the cathode and chlorine at the anode. Introductory ion-discharge notation describes these as H⁺ and Cl⁻ discharge. The cathode process is more directly written 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen forms at the cathode and chlorine at the anode. Introductory ion-discharge notation describes these as H⁺ and Cl⁻ discharge. The cathode process is more directly written 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For CO(g) + H₂O(g) → CO₂(g) + H₂(g), calculate ΔH° using formation enthalpies CO₂(g) = −394, H₂O(g) = −242 and CO(g) = −110 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.ai_explanation: Use products minus reactants: ΔH° = [−394 + 0] − [−110 + (−242)] = −42 kJ mol⁻¹. Hydrogen in its standard elemental state has zero standard enthalpy of formation.
questions.explanation: Use products minus reactants: ΔH° = [−394 + 0] − [−110 + (−242)] = −42 kJ mol⁻¹. Hydrogen in its standard elemental state has zero standard enthalpy of formation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed sample conducts electricity through mobile ions under the stated conditions?
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium acetate solution contains mobile Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ ions. Solid KOH has ions fixed in a lattice; mercury conducts through electrons rather than electrolytic ion movement.
questions.explanation: Sodium acetate solution contains mobile Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ ions. Solid KOH has ions fixed in a lattice; mercury conducts through electrons rather than electrolytic ion movement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Many characteristic transition-metal properties arise from partly filled subshells in their atoms or ions of type
questions.ai_explanation: Many transition-metal properties arise from incompletely filled d subshells in their atoms or common ions. These states help explain variable oxidation states and many coloured complexes.
